questions.prompt: Trapezoid ABCD has AB ∥ DC. M and N are the midpoints of legs AD and BC. Prove that MN ∥ AB and MN = ½(AB + DC).
questions.prompt_markup: Trapezoid ABCD has AB ∥ DC. M and N are the midpoints of legs AD and BC. Prove that MN ∥ AB and MN = ½(AB + DC).
questions.correct_answer: MN ∥ AB and MN = ½(AB + DC)
questions.required_method: Draw diagonal AC; let P be the midpoint of AC; use the midsegment theorem (or the converse) in △ACD and △ABC.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: in △ADC, MP ∥ DC and MP = ½DC; in △ABC, PN ∥ AB and PN = ½AB; AB ∥ DC so MP and PN are both parallel to AB through P, so M, P, N are collinear; MN = ½(AB + DC).
